Applicant has filed second bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 on behalf of the applicant for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.58/2021 registered at P.S. STF Bhopal, Unit Ujjain (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 419, 420,
467, 468 and 471, 34 of IPC read with Section 66-D of Information Technology Act.

He is in jail since 15.07.2022.
2.

As per the prosecution story, present applicant alongwith other co- accused on the basis of the fake Mail I.D. in the name of Capital Federation Company Investment Advisory and also prepared a forged invoice of the Said Company and sent the alleged forged invoice to complainant Avinash and committed cheating with the complainant of an amount of Rs.4,10,000/-.
Accordingly, a case has been registered.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.
Applicant is in jail since 15.07.2022.

His earlier bail application was dismissed on merit vide order dated 10.11.2022 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 43920/2022 but thereafter no-accused Hemant has been enlarged on bail vide order dated 18.4.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.
49454/2022, the entire amount in question of Rs. 4,10,000/- has been deposited by co-accused Hemant.
Final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.
Hence, he prays that in the changed circumstances, applicant be released on bail.
4. Per-contra, learned PL for respondent/State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.

5. Perused the case diary as well as the impugned order of the court below.
6.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for the parties, nature and gravity of allegation as also taking note of the fact that entire amount of Rs.
4,10,000/- has been deposited by co-accused Hemant and he has been enlarged on bail, the case of present applicant is identical to the case of co-accused Hemant and final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.
In view of the material changes in the circumstances, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Dipesh Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69117193/
